subject: Makegood pathway for Slate delay — exec signoff needed
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orbit accommodation request re: Slate timeline

Team — Orbit (contact: Katie Johnson) just escalated a request for a commercial accommodation. Their integration depends on the Slate prefetch cache landing in our runtime; engineering pushed the ship date by ~6 weeks (blocking one phase of their rollout). They say the delay materially increased their token spend and risk to their launch metrics.

Attached: Slate_Roadmap_Gap_Summary.pdf (short summary I pulled from Eng/Prod).

Customer ask (from their note): one-time credit to offset incremental token costs for 3 months OR a temporary discount on generation calls until the feature ships. They want a quick response and said this influences their finalize/close timeline.

Ask to the group:
- Marissa: please own the customer-facing proposal (numbers and tone).
- Karthik: can you quantify the P&L/ARR impact for several credit options (one-time vs monthly discount, caps).
- Laura: legal — any contract/precedent risks if we offer a makegood here?
- Monica: CS — does Orbit have other escalations we should factor into a broader remediation?

I think a limited, one-time makegood with clear expiration and acceptance criteria is the least risky path. If the team agrees, we need an exec signoff (Marcus or Finance) for anything > $20k. Holding off will jeopardize the renewal timing.

Rafael
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Slate_Roadmap_Gap_Summary.pdf (3 pages; highlights timing, impacted endpoints, estimated extra tokens/day)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbit accommodation request re: Slate timeline

Rafael — quick legal note:
- We can do a one-off credit or a capped temporary discount; prefer one-off credited to the account (reduces ongoing complexity).
- Avoid changing list prices or creating a precedent that applies broadly — mark the exception as an "operational accommodation tied to product delivery" and include acceptance language (customer acknowledges feature delay and accepts the credit in lieu of SLA remedies).
- If value > $25k, Legal wants a short amendment or acknowledgement doc. I can draft a two-paragraph addendum; should be quick.

Also attaching a short template SOW for makegood language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: proposed-makegood-SOW.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbit accommodation request re: Slate timeline

Team — ran a few scenarios based on Orbit's reported uplift. Numbers below are rounded.

Option A — One-time credit to cover 3 months of incremental spend: $42,000. Cap it at the reported overage and require reconciliation after 3 months. Estimated P&L hit: ~0.8% of this quarter's bookings if applied.
Option B — Temporary 20% discount on generation calls for up to 3 months: ~$55,000 revenue deferral (worse for short-term cashflow, cleaner for customer).
Option C — Smaller one-time credit plus service credit (e.g., $20k + free onboarding support): ~$28,000 immediate hit but preserves revenue.

Recommendation: Option C — gives Orbit tangible relief while keeping our exposure limited. If leadership approves Option C as an exception, I can model the amortization and refresh MRR impact. For anything above $25k we should queue exec approval (Marcus/Finance).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Katie Johnson <kjohnson@orbitapps.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jun 2028 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Accommodation request — proposed path forward

Katie — thanks for the candid note and for outlining the impact. We want Orbit to succeed and move this to a practical fix.

Proposed near-term accommodation (subject to internal signoff):
- One-time commercial credit of $20,000 applied to your account within 10 business days after agreement signing.
- Free priority onboarding and a technical review with our runtime team to optimize request patterns until Slate ships.
- Credit is a single use accommodation tied to the Slate delivery timeline; acceptance requires a short acknowledgement (we'll send).

If that sounds reasonable, Rafael will follow up with the internal paperwork and timeline. If Orbit prefers the 3-month cover option we can escalate for exec approval but it will take 24–48 hours to confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marcus — quick summary for signoff: Orbit (DEAL-8342) is asking for relief tied to a 6-week delay of the Slate prefetch cache. Customer will accept a $20k one-time credit plus a technical review; this preserves the renewal timeline. Finance (Karthik) modeled Option C as ~$28k exposure vs higher alternatives; Legal (Laura) recommends a short acknowledgement doc.

Attachment: proposed-makegood-SOW.docx; HubSpot link: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/8342

Request: approval to offer the $20,000 one-time credit under the standard acknowledgement (Legal will prepare). If approved, Marissa will send the paper and Rafael will coordinate application of the credit and the technical review sprint. Customer expects a signed doc from us by next Friday.

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY or a counter limit. If we need to go higher, we will escalate but want to avoid delaying the customer commitment.

Rafael
